column1: What type of change occurs when milk is left at room temperature during summers?
column2: A chemical change.

column1: What is the common observation when an iron tawa or nail is left exposed to a humid atmosphere?
column2: It undergoes a chemical change known as rusting.

column1: Whenever a chemical change occurs, we can say that a _____ has taken place.
column2: Chemical reaction

column1: Why is a magnesium ribbon rubbed with sandpaper before burning in air?
column2: To clean it and remove the protective layer of magnesium oxide from its surface.

column1: With what kind of flame does a magnesium ribbon burn?
column2: A dazzling white flame.

column1: What is the chemical name of the white powder formed after burning a magnesium ribbon?
column2: $Magnesium\ oxide$

column1: Magnesium oxide is formed due to the reaction between magnesium and _____ present in the air.
column2: Oxygen

column1: List the four main observations that help determine if a chemical reaction has taken place.
column2: Change in state, change in colour, evolution of a gas, and change in temperature.

column1: In a chemical equation, on which side are the reactants written?
column2: The left-hand side ($LHS$).

column1: What does the arrowhead in a chemical equation represent?
column2: The direction of the reaction toward the products.

column1: What is a 'skeletal chemical equation'?
column2: An unbalanced chemical equation where the mass is not the same on both sides.

column1: Why must a skeletal chemical equation be balanced?
column2: To satisfy the Law of Conservation of Mass.

column1: The Law of Conservation of Mass states that mass can neither be _____ nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
column2: Created

column1: What is the name of the method used to balance chemical equations by using the smallest whole number coefficients?
column2: Hit-and-trial method

column1: In a chemical equation, what does the symbol $(aq)$ signify?
column2: Aqueous (the reactant or product is present as a solution in water).

column1: Which symbol is used to indicate that water is used in the form of steam in a reaction?
In the reaction $3Fe(s) + 4H_{2}O(g) \rightarrow Fe_{3}O_{4}(s) + 4H_{2}(g)$, what is the physical state of $Fe_{3}O_{4}$?
column2: Solid

column1: Define a combination reaction.
column2: A reaction in which a single product is formed from two or more reactants.

column1: What is the common name for calcium oxide ($CaO$)?
column2: Quick lime

column1: What is the chemical name and formula for 'slaked lime'?
column2: $Calcium\ hydroxide$ ($Ca(OH)_{2}$)

column1: Why does the beaker feel hot when water is added to quick lime?
column2: The reaction is exothermic and releases a large amount of heat.

column1: Define an exothermic chemical reaction.
column2: A reaction in which heat is released along with the formation of products.

column1: Name the reaction: $CH_{4}(g) + 2O_{2}(g) \rightarrow CO_{2}(g) + 2H_{2}O(g) + Energy$.
column2: Burning of natural gas (an exothermic reaction).

column1: Why is respiration considered an exothermic process?
column2: Because glucose combines with oxygen in cells to provide energy for the body.

column1: The decomposition of vegetable matter into compost is an example of an _____ reaction.
column2: Exothermic

column1: Which substance is used for white-washing walls?
column2: A solution of slaked lime ($Calcium\ hydroxide$).

column1: What substance gives a shiny finish to walls 2-3 days after white-washing?
column2: $Calcium\ carbonate$ ($CaCO_{3}$)

column1: What is the chemical formula for marble?
column2: $CaCO_{3}$

column1: Define a decomposition reaction.
column2: A reaction in which a single reactant breaks down to give simpler products.

column1: What is thermal decomposition?
column2: A decomposition reaction carried out by heating.

column1: What is the original colour of ferrous sulphate crystals?
column2: Green

column1: Name the three products formed when ferrous sulphate crystals are heated.
column2: $Ferric\ oxide$, $sulphur\ dioxide$, and $sulphur\ trioxide$.

column1: What happens when calcium carbonate is heated?
column2: It decomposes into calcium oxide (lime) and carbon dioxide gas.

column1: Which decomposition product is used in the manufacture of cement?
column2: Calcium oxide ($CaO$)

column1: What is observed when lead nitrate powder is heated in a boiling tube?
column2: The emission of brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide ($NO_{2}$).

column1: In the electrolysis of water, bubbles are formed at both electrodes. What process is this?
column2: Electrolytic decomposition

column1: What colour does white silver chloride turn when placed in sunlight?
column2: Grey

column1: Which form of energy causes the decomposition of silver chloride into silver and chlorine?
column2: Sunlight (Light energy)

column1: Silver bromide behaves similarly to silver chloride in sunlight. What are these reactions used for?
column2: Black and white photography.

column1: Define an endothermic reaction.
column2: A reaction in which energy is absorbed.

column1: What change is observed in the blue colour of copper sulphate solution when an iron nail is dipped in it?
column2: The blue colour fades.

column1: Define a displacement reaction.
column2: A reaction where a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound.

column1: Why does iron displace copper from copper sulphate solution?
column2: Iron is more reactive than copper.

column1: In the reaction $Zn(s) + CuSO_{4}(aq) \rightarrow ZnSO_{4}(aq) + Cu(s)$, which element is displaced?
column2: Copper

column1: What is a double displacement reaction?
column2: A reaction in which there is an exchange of ions between the reactants.

column1: What is a precipitate?
column2: An insoluble substance formed during a chemical reaction.

column1: Name the white precipitate formed when sodium sulphate reacts with barium chloride.
column2: $Barium\ sulphate$ ($BaSO_{4}$)

column1: Define oxidation in terms of oxygen gain/loss.
column2: The gain of oxygen by a substance during a reaction.

column1: Define reduction in terms of oxygen gain/loss.
column2: The loss of oxygen by a substance during a reaction.

column1: What is a redox reaction?
column2: A reaction where one reactant gets oxidised while the other gets reduced.

column1: When copper powder is heated, it becomes coated with a black substance. What is this substance?
column2: $Copper(II)\ oxide$

column1: How can the black coating of copper oxide be turned back into brown copper?
column2: By passing hydrogen gas over the heated copper oxide.

column1: Define oxidation in terms of hydrogen.
column2: The loss of hydrogen by a substance.

column1: Define reduction in terms of hydrogen.
column2: The gain of hydrogen by a substance.

column1: What is corrosion?
column2: The process where a metal is attacked by substances like moisture or acids around it.

column1: What is the colour of the coating formed on silver when it corrodes?
column2: Black

column1: What is the colour of the coating formed on copper due to corrosion?
column2: Green

column1: Define rancidity.
column2: The condition produced by the oxidation of fats and oils in food, resulting in unpleasant smell and taste.

column1: Why do chips manufacturers flush bags of chips with nitrogen gas?
column2: To prevent the chips from getting oxidised.

column1: What are antioxidants used for in the food industry?
column2: They are added to foods containing fats and oils to prevent oxidation.
